items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: So George Wein, who is not an Art Hodes fan, by any stretch of the imagination, gets me because there's some opening he has to fill.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's right. Who's the guy that writes about you? Who's the guy that books you? How do you find out, when you're talking to a booker who was a violin player, never liked jazz, couldn't stand it? Do you think he's going to plug it? No, man, I'm going to plug rock 'n roll, because that's where the money is. Art, I'm sorry, I like you as a person, there's nothing in the world I won't do for you. And unfortunately, there's nothing I can do for you. I'll do

nothing. And this gets to be a big laugh. So you do it for yourself, to the best of your ability. But as you say, it's gotten better. You can play a festival. You can go occasionally to Europe. You get lucky, you do something friendly like you did for Harriet Choice of the Tribune. In return, she turns out and talks to George Wein, you've got to get him one time. So George Wein, who is not an Art Hodes fan, by any stretch of the imagination, gets me because there's some opening he has to fill.

I get to Europe because of him. And there's two fellows that are booking singles that hear me. That's the sequence of events. So they heard me and they says, hey, man, will you come over for me? So that means three weeks working in Europe, three and a half. There's a man in England that won't book me, unfortunately. Now, he's booking all these other people, but to tell you the truth, he won't pay me what I can get going to Germany for this other man. He just -- I don't know what, in Europe he says, England is a…
